excerpt: "git blame" for LLM agent decisions: replay one recorded LLM request with pieces of context removed and report which chunk caused the decision. Works with any model: the evidence comes from replays, not from the model's own explanation. Status: v0.2.2, validated on open models (see docs/WRITEUP.md). v0.2.1 added correct chunking of Claude Code–style traces and audits reported causes on fresh replays (family-wise error ≤ α). v0.2.2 tells a rule that makes the agent act and picks what it does from one that only makes it act, by replaying with the tool forced. uvx ctxblame --help # or: pip install ctxblame Real v0.2.1 trace (real/run1/step21, Qwen3-14B on local vLLM): ctxblame separates the edit_file precondition, catches all 3 redundant --tb=line carriers that leave-one-out misses (5/5 kept alone), and certifies the bundle on 20 fresh replays (p = 1.9e-6, 91% KV-cache hit). The examples below use uv run ctxblame from a checkout; uvx ctxblame works the same. Two wire formats are supported, which covers most models: Anthropic Messages (/v1/messages) and OpenAI Chat Completions (/chat/completions). The simplest way is to wrap the agent command: uv run ctxblame wrap -- claude -p "fix the failing test" # or any agent command wrap starts two recording proxies on free local ports (Anthropic and OpenAI format) and runs the command with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and OPENAI_BASE_URL pointing at them. Base URLs you have already set become the upstreams, so an agent pointed at DeepSeek or a local vLLM server keeps using it (or pass --anthropic-upstream / --openai-upstream). The proxies stop when the command exits, and wrap exits with the command's code. Only clients that read these variables are captured; calls to other APIs (e.g. the OpenAI Responses API) are forwarded but not recorded.
